stemMd: According to the passage, which of the following is one of the costs that the operator of Ostria's deposit-return scheme has to meet?
instructionsMd: Answer on the basis of the passage only.

options.label: A
options.textMd: A fee paid to drinks producers for every container they put on the market

options.label: B
options.textMd: Payments to recyclers for taking away the collected material

options.label: C
options.textMd: A fee paid to a shop for each empty container the shop accepts

options.label: D
options.textMd: The cost of emptying the region's kerbside recycling bins

explanationMd:
Explicit-information questions are settled by finding the one sentence that answers them and reading it closely. Here it is the second sentence of the second paragraph, which lists the operator's costs: "the return machines, the counting centres, transport and a handling fee of €0.03 that it pays a shop for each container the shop accepts". A fee paid to a shop for each container it accepts is one of those costs, stated in so many words.

**How to check the answer.** The same sentence goes on to list the three sources of **income**: sales of material to recyclers, a fee charged to producers, and unclaimed deposits. Two of the wrong choices take an item from that income list and turn its direction around, so that money flowing to the operator is described as money flowing out of it. Test each choice by asking which way the money moves in the passage, not just whether the same words appear.

distractorRationale.a: The passage mentions a producer fee, but it runs the other way: it is "a fee charged to producers for every container they put on the market", one of the operator's sources of income. This choice reverses the direction of the payment.
distractorRationale.b: Recyclers do not get paid by the operator; they pay it. The passage lists "the sale of the collected material to recyclers" as a source of income. This choice turns a sale into a cost.
distractorRationale.d: Kerbside bins appear only in the first paragraph, as the way containers were collected before the scheme. Nothing in the passage makes the operator responsible for them, so this cost is imported from outside the text.

accessibilityText: A question about the accompanying passage on Ostria's deposit-return scheme for drinks containers. It asks which of four items the passage names as one of the costs the scheme's operator has to meet. The four choices, in the order shown, are: a fee paid to drinks producers for every container they put on the market; a fee paid to a shop for each empty container the shop accepts; payments to recyclers for taking away the collected material; the cost of emptying the region's kerbside recycling bins.

provenance.notes: Original explicit-detail item on the original passage bocconi-ug-stim-deposit-return-546. Two distractors reverse the direction of a payment that the passage lists as income; the third imports a cost the passage never assigns to the operator.
